title: Moss Mysteries
solvedCount: No case solved yet | 1 case solved | {count} cases solved
clueRevealed: A new clue is waiting in Moss Mysteries. | {count} new clues are waiting in Moss Mysteries.
intro: Someone has been found dead in a house full of guests. Each task you complete reveals one clue about where everyone stood. Work out the whole floor plan, then name the murderer. Your first case comes with every clue already revealed.
off: Moss Mysteries is off, so completed tasks reveal no clues.

rules.title: How to play
rules.grid: Everyone stands on exactly one square, and no two people share a row or a column: each row and each column holds one person.
rules.murderer: The victim’s name starts with V, and nobody else’s does. Their room holds exactly two people: the victim and the murderer. Nobody else is ever alone with the victim.
rules.furniture: Armchairs, sofas and beds are seats: someone can stand there. Every other piece of furniture fills its square, so nobody stands on it.
rules.directions: North is the top of the plan and west is its left. “Next to” means sharing a side, in the same room: a wall in between or touching at a corner does not count. “Exactly 2 rows further north” counts rows only, whatever the column, “the very next square to the north” is the one just above, and “exactly 3 squares to the north” stays in the same column, whatever stands between.
rules.terms: A corner square is one of the four corners of the plan. Someone is in a corner of a room when their square touches a wall or the edge of the plan both to the north or south and to the east or west. Two people are on the same diagonal when their squares line up at 45°, either way. “Alone” means nobody else was in their room; “alone with a woman” means exactly one other person was there, a woman; “shared a room with a man in a bed” means another person in their room, a man, was in a bed. “In a room with a piano” means a piano stood somewhere in their room. “The only person in a bed” means nobody else, the victim included, was in a bed anywhere on the plan. “Further north than a piano” means in a row further north than at least one piano, whatever the column; east and west count columns the same way. “At least 3 people were in the library” counts the victim too.
rules.counts: A room’s head count includes the victim: “Nobody was in the kitchen” means the victim was not there either, and “Exactly 3 people were in the library” counts the victim among them.
rules.clues: There is one clue per person. The victim’s, alone with the murderer, is given from the start; each task you complete reveals the next one. A clue can join two facts: the second is about the same person, except after “alone with a woman” or “alone with a man”, where it is about that one other person, or it is about a room.
rules.board: The board rules, above the clues, hold for the whole plan and are known from the start.
rules.marks: Pick a person, then tap a square to place them. With nobody picked, tap an empty square to cross it out, or tap a placed person to take them back off. Your marks are saved with the case.
rules.accusation: Once everyone is placed, choose the murderer and accuse. A wrong accusation costs nothing and does not say what is wrong.
